stories.title: Your agent trusts the vendor docs more than you do
stories.blurb: Researchers scanned 6,214 domains and found 8,265 llms.txt files, 120 of which pointed at package names nobody had registered. They claimed a handful, and within an hour a Fortune 500 machine phoned home. The parent-process chain named Claude, Codex and Hermes: coding agents read setup docs as ground truth and install what they are told to install.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Claude, Codex, and Hermes installed unowned code inside corporate networks

stories.title: The designer who discovered she was the one in the wrong lane
stories.blurb: Kelly Smith spent months honking at other drivers on a Newcastle roundabout before Google Maps settled the argument against her. Her point is not the embarrassment but the pattern: the junction is an accident black spot, and a Norman door taken at thirty miles an hour is a design problem, not a driver problem.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: The Smith Roundabout; or, the shame of being the cutter-upper

stories.title: Häagen-Dazs stops showing the bite and starts showing the coating
stories.blurb: Landor's new stick packaging for France and the UK drops the category's cracked-chocolate convention, which borrows its look from an ice cream someone has already bitten. The chocolate now drapes rather than covers, the burgundy runs across the whole pack, and vertical stripes carry range recognition on shelf.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Landor reimagines Häagen-Dazs ice cream stick packaging around desire, texture and taste

stories.title: Somebody picked the bird logo back up off the floor
stories.blurb: Operation Bluebird has relaunched Twitter at twitter.now, arguing the trademark was abandoned when the platform became X in 2022. One founder ran trademarks and domain names at the original Twitter until 2016. X is suing in Delaware, and a tentative ruling in April suggested Bluebird may have a case.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: The return of Twitter could be a happy ending after the worst rebrand of all time

stories.title: The one restrained cover in a studio built on the surreal
stories.blurb: Wiedemann Lampe have curated five decades of George Hardie for the London Design Festival, drawn partly from work Benji Wiedemann found at Hardie's home in West Sussex. His reading of Dark Side of the Moon is the useful part: made inside Hipgnosis, yet rational and restrained where the house style was fantastical.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: George Hardie's five-decade career celebrated in new London Design Festival exhibition

stories.title: An LED is the whole consent mechanism, and it had a loophole
stories.blurb: Meta will stop the camera when the recording light is covered mid-capture, closing a bypass that only required reversing the order of two steps. EU regulators are probing whether the light was ever field-tested for bystander comprehension, Germany is weighing a ban, and a US class action over the privacy marketing is advancing.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording

stories.title: A rendering layer that repaints the frame after the artists are done
stories.blurb: DLSS 5 Neural Rendering files turned up in an early-access build of NBA 2K27 and modders have pointed them at Control and Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth. Foliage holds up; faces do not. The interesting part is what the leak exposes, since none of these games had lighting or materials tuned for a system that intervenes after rendering.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: "Unsettling" – Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 AI filter has leaked, and gamers are horrified

stories.title: Neither side gets to see the other's homework
stories.blurb: DeepMind is piloting a double-blind evaluation of a Gemini Flash Lite model with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, running tests inside Confidential Space so the evaluator never sees the weights and Google never sees the prompts. It targets benchmark contamination, the reason a good score currently proves less than it looks.

sources.name: Google DeepMind
sources.headline: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations
